title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is studying the 'équation des lacets' scheme-theoretically. Over a base W (or S) he has a rank-2 locally free module F and two automorphisms ρ, σ of F. They are meant to be fibrewise conjugate to the standard generators of SL(2,Z): σ0 = [[0,-1],[1,0]] of order 4, and ρ0 = [[0,1],[-1,1]] of order 6. They are subject to the condition that ε0 = -σ^{-1}ρ (and ε1 = -ρσ^{-1}) be unipotent, mirroring the amalgam SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 with ε0 = [[1,-1],[0,1]]. Earlier he had listed conditions (51)-(56) for this.

Remark on this page. He suspects most of (51)-(56) are superabundant. He proposes to replace them by simple algebraic identities, (64): σ^2+1 = 0, ρ^2-ρ+1 = 0, (ρ+σ)^2 = ρ+σ. A marginal NB says he must specify which of Tr σ=0, det σ=1, Tr ρ=1, det ρ=1 are implied or must be added.

The third identity says N := ρ+σ is idempotent, (65)-(66). Since σ^{-1} = -σ, one gets (67): ε0 = σρ = 1-σ^{-1}N = 1+N0 with N0 = σN, and symmetrically ε1 = 1+N1 with N1 = Nσ. 'ε0 unipotent' (nontrivially unipotent on each fibre) becomes (68): det σN = Tr σN = 0 and σN nonzero on fibres, i.e. N nonzero on fibres.

He shows the non-vanishing is automatic. Work over a field. If N = 0 then ρ = -σ, so σ^2+1 = 0 and σ^2+σ+1 = 0, hence σ = 0, which is absurd. If N = 1 then σ = 1-ρ, which gives ρ^2-2ρ+2 = 0. Subtracting ρ^2-ρ+1 = 0 gives ρ = 1, and then 1 = 0 (finished on the next page).

Hence N is fibrewise a nonzero proper idempotent, i.e. a rank-1 projector. Locally N = x'⊗x with <x,x'> = 1, so Tr N = 1 and det N = 0, and det σN = 0 is automatic. On the next page he reduces everything to Tr σN = 0, i.e. Tr σρ = 2, and asks whether this follows from the rest.

Purpose. He wants a clean, small system of polynomial equations defining the scheme of 'lacets' (pairs (ρ,σ) realising the SL2(Z) amalgam relation), on which GL(2)_S acts with stabilisers N'_ρ, N'_σ (previous page). Geometrically, the idempotent N = ρ+σ rigidifies the data by a splitting F = Im N ⊕ Ker N into lines; for the standard pair, ρ0+σ0 = diag(0,1).
errors: First equation label: the image reads (64), not (69); the following labels run (65)-(68), and (69) is used on the next page for Tr σρ = 2.

Gap he himself flags in the margin: σ^2+1 = 0 and ρ^2-ρ+1 = 0 do not imply Tr σ = 0, det σ = 1, Tr ρ = 1, det ρ = 1. Over a field containing i, σ = i·Id satisfies σ^2 = -1 with det σ = -1; in characteristic 2, σ = Id works. So the trace/determinant conditions (fibrewise 'regular', non-scalar) must be imposed separately.

The question left open on the next page (is Tr σρ = 2 a consequence of the other relations?) has an immediate positive answer, given Tr σ = 0 and Tr ρ = 1. The polarised Cayley-Hamilton identity for 2x2 matrices, AB+BA = Tr(A)B + Tr(B)A + (Tr(AB) - Tr A·Tr B)·1, gives ρσ+σρ = σ + Tr(ρσ)·1. Hence (ρ+σ)^2 = ρ-1+ρσ+σρ-1 = ρ+σ iff Tr(ρσ) = 2, over any base ring. So, once the trace/det conditions are added, N^2 = N is equivalent to Tr σρ = 2, which then gives Tr σN = 0 at once. Grothendieck's detour through the rank-1 projector is correct but unnecessary for this point.
Minor: 'σ = 0, absurde' is correct (σ^2 = -1 then gives 0 = -1).

ideas.what: Replace the unipotence condition on ε0 = -σ^{-1}ρ by the idempotence of N = ρ+σ, for ρ, σ with σ^2 = -1 and ρ^2-ρ+1 = 0 in rank 2 over an arbitrary base
ideas.modern_name: Polynomial presentation of the representation scheme of SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 into GL2 / SL2 (character-variety style equations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical matrix identity (ρ0+σ0 = diag(0,1)); representation/character varieties of free products: Culler-Shalen, Lubotzky-Magid (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Only in these 'Longue Marche' sequel notes as far as known

ideas.what: Fibrewise argument that the idempotent N is neither 0 nor 1, hence a locally split rank-1 projector N = x'⊗x with Tr N = 1, det N = 0
ideas.modern_name: Rank-1 idempotent / splitting of a rank-2 bundle into lines

ideas.what: Programme of finding a minimal, non-superabundant set of algebraic equations for the 'lacets' data over Spec Z, with the GL(2) action and stabilisers N'_ρ, N'_σ
ideas.modern_name: Integral model of the SL2(Z)-representation scheme / moduli of 'framed' SL2(Z)-structures

missed.claim: Grothendieck's open question whether Tr σρ = 2 follows from the other relations is answered by the polarised Cayley-Hamilton identity: it is equivalent to (ρ+σ)^2 = ρ+σ once traces and determinants are fixed. The defining system therefore collapses to σ^2 = -1, ρ^2-ρ+1 = 0, Tr σ = 0, Tr ρ = 1 (det conditions follow by Cayley-Hamilton) plus Tr σρ = 2, valid over Spec Z. This is a small, essentially routine completion.
missed.quote: Rmq J'ai la nette impression que la plupart des conditions (51) à (56) sont surabondantes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It gives a clean integral presentation of the scheme of pairs realising the SL2(Z) amalgam relation, but this is standard for anyone writing equations of representation varieties.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine linear-algebra simplification of defining equations, with a correct but slightly roundabout argument. The open question it raises is settled by a standard trace identity. Nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Equation label on the first displayed formula is (64), not (69).
Margin: the trace condition on ρ should read Tr ρ = 1, not Tr ρ = 0 (ρ^2-ρ+1 = 0); the handwriting is ambiguous.
'(ou définition [?] ε0 p. (51))' is better read as '(cf. définition de ε0 par (51))'.
'on pourrait si W est spectre d'un corps' should read roughly 'on pourrait supposer W spectre d'un corps'.
Header number '469' is Grothendieck's own pagination.
